newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert to buy Esselte out of JV.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert to buy Esselte out of JV.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV said on Thursday it planned to buy out Swedish retailing and office equipment company Esselte AB of their Innovative Sputtering Technology NV joint venture after IST sales to Esselte fell in 1996.
Esselte is the main customer for IST's anti-shoplifting devices employing sputtered films.

"Sales to the joint venture partner were less than we had anticipated. We will become the 100 percent owner of this company and are developing new products," Bekaert chief executive officer Raf Decaluwe told a news conference.
Bekaert presently owns 80 percent of IST, while Esselte holds 20 percent.
Bekaert said the transaction should be completed in the course of 1997. Terms were not disclosed.
The IST sputtered films venture forms part of Bekaert's "new activities" division, which the company hopes will become an engine for future earnings growth.
At the start of 1996 Bekaert said the outlook for sputtered films remained very positive and began work on constructing a new plant in the United States.
However, while "new activities" sales rose 15 percent in 1996, sputtered film sales slipped 10 percent.
Bekaert said its new U.S. factory in North Carolina, which will in addition to serving IST also make fibres used in airbags, should start production around summer 1997.
